correctness.rationale: If two ordinary vertices in either clique are white, neither can be first forced, giving the two threshold necessities. At both thresholds with both bridge endpoints white there is no initial force. In every other threshold-satisfying case one clique can be completed, then the bridge endpoint forces across and the other clique completes. Independent inclusion-exclusion gives the displayed four coefficients. The inspected verifier exhaustively checks all \(3\le a,b\le7\), and an independent brute-force reconstruction matched the formula at \((3,3),(3,4),(4,5)\).

originality.rationale: The foundational zero-forcing-polynomial paper develops family formulas and explicitly leaves splitting formulas across cut vertices or separating sets as an open direction. Menon--Singh give coefficientwise inequalities under graph operations, and later path-extremal work gives bounds, not this bridge-barbell all-set classification. value.rationale: Bridge barbells are a basic cut-edge composition of two dense blocks, precisely the kind of separating-set setting highlighted by the foundational polynomial paper. The exact all-set threshold rule and closed polynomial provide a natural test case for future splitting formulas, not an arbitrary finite slice.

final_claim: For the bridge barbell \(B_{a,b}\), \(a,b\ge3\), a set is zero forcing exactly under the two clique-threshold conditions with the single excluded double-threshold endpoint-free configuration; consequently \(\mathcal Z(B_{a,b};x)=x^{a+b-3}(x^3+(a+b)x^2+(ab+a+b-2)x+(2ab-a-b))\).
limitations: Single bridge joining two cliques of orders at least three.
No general bridge-splitting theorem for arbitrary graphs is claimed.
